newsitem.title: USA: Winter storm cuts power to 180,000 in Houston.
newsitem.headline: Winter storm cuts power to 180,000 in Houston.

text.p: Houston Lighting and Power Co said 180,000 customers were without electric power on Monday as a winter storm passing through south Texas coated trees and power lines with a heavy coating of ice.

Most of the outages were in wooded suburbs north and west of Houston, where tree limbs and power lines were snapping under the weight of ice from freezing rain overnight, HL&P spokesman Graham Painter said.
"As soon as the line crews were able to get one circuit back on, another would go off," Painter said.

With temperatures hovering near freezing and forecasts calling for an 80 percent chance of more rain and sleet, the Houston utility expected rolling outages to continue through the day and into Tuesday.
Additional crews were dispatched to the northern and western suburbs to clear fallen tree limbs and power lines to restore power in those hardest hit areas, Painter said.
"I don't know if it's going to get better any time soon," he said. "We're going to have another night of it, at least."
